title: private-cohort-scheduler-and-preflight-catalog
creator: Liam Chen
description: Build a cohort-based scheduler and a pluggable preflight catalog to run staged, reversible upgrades for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). The goal is to provide: (1) tenant/cohort grouping and sequencing for canary and progressive rollouts, (2) a catalog of preflight probes (schema compatibility, KV cache warmability, model binary compatibility, network path checks), (3) an operator-driven migration runner that executes database schema changes and config transitions with transactional checkpoints and automated rollbacks, and (4) integration with Console rollout gates and telemetry for automated pass/fail decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Cohort scheduler can define and persist at least three rollout cohorts per deployment (canary, early-adopter, general) and reorder cohorts via API
Preflight catalog exposes at least five probe types (schema-compatibility, config-diff, storage-check, kv-cache-warm, runtime-compat-check) and can run in dry-run mode
Migration runner supports dry-run, apply, and rollback modes; preserves snapshot markers for transactional recovery
Console shows cohort progress and a per-cohort gate status tied to telemetry (error-rate, p99 latency, success-rate) and prevents next cohort unless pass criteria met
End-to-end test harness verifies rollback on injected failure and completes within SLO for upgrade window in staging
design_decisions: Persist cohort definitions as CRDs in the on-prem control plane to avoid dependence on external state stores
Preflight probes are implemented as containerized plugins with a standardized input/output contract (stdin JSON / stdout JSON) so customers can add custom probes
Use migration checkpoints with immutable IDs and a two-phase apply (prepare + commit) to enable deterministic rollback
Gate evaluation will be rule-based in Console but extensible to ML-based anomaly detectors in a follow-up project
All networked actions from the private control plane will use mTLS to customer-managed endpoints and log to audit trails for compliance
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag behind 'private.upgrade.cohort' for all Private clusters; internal smoke tests
Phase 1: Internal canary on Redwood-managed VPC customers (low risk) with preflight catalog enabled
Phase 2: Invitelist early-adopter customer cohorts with operator-assisted runs and 24/7 oncall coverage
Phase 3: Gradual automated progression to general cohort with gate checks (24h observation per cohort) and automatic pause on regressions
Phase 4: GA release and docs + runbook published to customers and Solutions Engineers
risks: Long-running migrations could overlap with customer traffic patterns causing transient latency spikes
Insufficient probe coverage may miss compatibility regressions for edge-case tenant configs
Rollback semantics for non-idempotent migrations require careful handling (e.g., data backfills)
Operator upgrades themselves must be backward compatible with older control-plane agents during rollout
On-prem environments with strict egress rules may block probe container downloads; need offline probe package support
testing_notes: Integration harness in CI will simulate 3 tenant cohorts with phase-shifted traffic patterns and inject failure in cohort-2 to validate pause + rollback
We added a staging job that runs the preflight catalog against the latest release artifacts for every week-night build
Load tests will verify that snapshotting and checkpoint db writes do not exceed 5% of normal request tail latency
Manual dry-run: run migration runner in 'plan-only' mode and verify no persistent schema changes are applied
